html:
The Darumbal are the Aboriginal Australian people of the Rockhampton area of central Queensland, on the lower Fitzroy River and the coast of Keppel Bay. They speak dialects of the Darumbal language.

Their neighbours were the Guwinmal to the north, the Gangulu and Gabalbara inland and the Bayali to the south.

Squatters reached the Fitzroy in the mid 1850s. A gold rush at Canoona in 1858 brought thousands of miners, and the town of Rockhampton was founded the same year as the river port. The frontier around it was violent, with the Native Police active in the district.
